races.name: Stonepack Mares' 'National Hunt' Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Bracing Brook
runners_data.note: Hold-up style mare making hurdle debut for in-form Henderson yard, but 162 days off and was pulled up on only previous start
runners_data.comment: 500-1 when pulled up on debut in a novice hurdle at Ayr (2m, soft) last November
runners_data.spotlight: Dam 3m hurdle winner (RPR 89); 500-1 when pulled up on debut in a novice hurdle at Ayr (2m, soft) last November; hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Quinnfinity
runners_data.note: Unraced and unknown style, Mike Smith yard struggling with 0/8 in last 14 days, impossible to assess
runners_data.comment: 6,000euros 3yo; half-sister to two winners but probably best watched on debut
runners_data.spotlight: 6,000euros 3yo; seventh foal; half-sister to winners Lone Wolf (bumper/useful 2m2f hurdle) and Love At Sea (bumper/2m1f hurdle); dam dual point winner; she's probably best watched on debut.

runners_data.name: Celtic Alliance
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with strong RPR 125 debut win, Elliott's 6/52 record provides confidence for step up in class
runners_data.comment: Won 4yo maiden hurdle at Clonmel three weeks ago on her sole start; major player
runners_data.spotlight: 7-1 when winning on debut in a 4yo maiden hurdle at Clonmel (2m, soft) three weeks ago; this half-sister to the yard's useful 2m3f/2m4f hurdle winner Absolute Notions is a bright prospect and, in conjunction with stablemate Dunsy Rock, has the best form in the field.

runners_data.name: Dunsy Rock
runners_data.note: Prominent runner ideally positioned to track the leader, proven form on good going and 6-length last win shows class
runners_data.comment: Won at Fairyhouse in February; leading form claims, along with stablemate Celtic Alliance
runners_data.spotlight: Built upon the promise of her debut run at Down Royal (2m4f, yielding) in December to win by 6l in a big field at Fairyhouse (2m, heavy) in February; leading form claims, along with her stablemate Celtic Alliance.

runners_data.name: Viscountess Nelson
runners_data.note: Hold-up style point winner who was close second on hurdle debut, Henderson's 8/29 record suggests readiness
runners_data.comment: Plumpton runner-up; something to find with the Elliott runners but open to improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner who built upon her bumper debut fourth when 1l runner-up at Plumpton (2m4f, good to soft) last month on her first hurdle start; she has something to find with the Gordon Elliott runners but is in top hands and open to improvement.

runners_data.name: Frankies Fortune
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner returning after 164 days, claiming jockey reduces weight but adds inexperience factor
runners_data.comment: Point winner; needs to improve upon her bumper form to make an impact on hurdle debut
runners_data.spotlight: Won Irish mares' maiden point (3m, yielding) on debut last April and ran okay when fifth in Carlisle bumper (2m1f, good) in October; tailed off there (2m1f, soft) the following month; should come good at some point but she's in a warm race for her hurdle debut and others are preferred.

runners_data.name: Sagonige
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with terrible recent form but showed ability in points, question marks over retained ability after long absence
runners_data.comment: Tailed off on both hurdle starts, after a long absence; promising in bumpers in 2023-24
runners_data.spotlight: Tailed off this year on first two hurdle starts, following a long absence; there's a big question mark about how much ability she retains but she showed promise in bumpers in 2023-24 and might not be a forlorn hope each-way.

runners_data.name: Oor Wish
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare making hurdle debut after disappointing bumper form this year, trainer's 1/10 record offers little hope
runners_data.comment: Bred to be suited by step up in trip on hurdle debut but still likely she'll come up short
runners_data.spotlight: Big odds and unable to pose a threat this year on her three bumper starts (heavy-good to soft); bred to be suited by the step up in trip on hurdle debut but it still seems likely she'll come up short.

runners_data.name: Aristelle
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with 10-pound claimer aboard, mixed form but showed ability in December Carlisle bumper third
runners_data.comment: Displayed ability in one of her bumpers but tailed off at 50-1 on recent hurdle debut
runners_data.spotlight: Displayed ability when third in a bumper at Carlisle (2m1f, soft) in December but tailed off at Newcastle (2m, AW) next time and same story when 50-1 for recent hurdle debut at Carlisle (2m3f, good to soft).

races.paceDynamic: Frankies Fortune is the lone confirmed front-runner in this field and will dictate terms from the start, likely setting a sustainable gallop without pressure from other pace angles. With most runners adopting hold-up tactics (Bracing Brook, Celtic Alliance, Viscountess Nelson, Sagonige, Oor Wish, Aristelle) and only Dunsy Rock showing prominent tendencies, the pace will be measured through the early stages. This creates a tactical race where positioning becomes crucial, as horses will need to find racing room in the straight when the pace lifts. This race shape clearly favours prominent runners who can track the pace and hold-up horses with a strong finishing kick, as they'll benefit from the steady gallop and have first run on those settling further back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Measured Pace Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Frankies Fortune sets uncontested fractions and the field bunches up
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace will suit the strong closers who can quicken off the bend. Celtic Alliance and Viscountess Nelson can use their proven finishing kicks to maximum effect.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Dunsy Rock tracks Frankies Fortune in second and controls the race
scenarios.body: Her prominent style perfectly suits this scenario as she can dictate when to quicken. The Elliott-trained mare has the tactical speed to kick clear before the hold-up horses can respond.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Frankies Fortune maintains her gallop and the field fails to quicken
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows her to save enough for the finish on this stamina test. Her point-to-point background over longer trips gives her the staying power others may lack.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is too slow and multiple horses challenge simultaneously
scenarios.body: A messy finish develops where positioning and racing room become crucial factors. The jockeys with the best judgement will find the clearest passage in a bunched finish.

watchPoints.text: Frankies Fortune's fitness after 164 days off - if she fades in the straight, it transforms the race dynamics completely
Track Dunsy Rock's position turning for home - if she's travelling well in second, she becomes very hard to pass
Celtic Alliance's jumping under pressure - any mistakes at the business end could cost her the race despite her class edge
Watch for traffic problems in the straight given the number of hold-up runners - clear passage will be at a premium
Monitor Viscountess Nelson's position at the second-last hurdle - she needs to be in the first four to deliver her proven finishing kick

runners_data.name: A King Of Magic
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong recent Taunton form but faces significant tactical disadvantage against this field of fellow back-markers
runners_data.comment: He's shaped as though he'll be suited by the step up in trip; lots to like on h'cap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Won in a first-time tongue-tie (retained since) at Taunton (2m, heavy) in February on second hurdle start and went close at Sedgefield (2m1f, good) last month; he's shaped as though he'll be suited by the step up in trip and there's lots to like on his handicap debut.

runners_data.name: King Jon Oliver
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose forward style suits this tactical setup, though Murphy's yard is below-par recently
runners_data.comment: The drop back down in trip could help and his trainer has a good record in this race
runners_data.spotlight: Won on stable debut at Fakenham (2m4f, good to soft) in January and bounced back from heavy-ground flop on handicap debut at Hereford when fourth at Uttoxeter (2m7f, good to soft) last month; shaped last time as though this shorter trip would help and trainer has a good record in this race.

runners_data.name: Bois Guillbert
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from 81-day break to a lower mark but faces traffic problems with his running style
runners_data.comment: On a dangerous mark but has struggled over fences/hurdles on his three runs this season
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time hurdle winner who has dropped to a mark 5lb lower than when winning on his chase debut last February; he may stage a revival at some stage but has struggled over fences/hurdles on his three runs this season.

runners_data.name: Kingston Narcissus
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose tactical approach is ideal for this scenario, though tongue-tie form has been mixed lately
runners_data.comment: Won at Sedgefield in December but two lesser performances have followed
runners_data.spotlight: Won in a first-time tongue-tie (retained since) at Sedgefield (2m4f, good to soft) in December; however, two lesser performances have followed (2m3f/2m5f, soft/good to soft) and he needs to get back on track.

runners_data.name: Joeybottles
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who gets perfect setup with sustainable pace and no early pressure from this field composition
runners_data.comment: Easy win on last month's handicap debut at Bangor and a 10lb rise may not stop him
runners_data.spotlight: Ran well in a bumper here last April on debut (good to soft) and, having had wind surgery, he made a winning handicap debut at 9-2 at Bangor (2m3f, good) last month; did it easily and a 10lb rise may not stop him.

runners_data.name: Platin Moon
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse switching from front-running tactics, creating uncertainty about positioning while Bruce Lynn takes the ride
runners_data.comment: Front-runner who has won two of his last three starts; further improvement is possible
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who won at Ayr (2m, heavy) in January before solid third at Musselburgh (1m7f, good to soft), and he won again at Ayr (2m, soft) last month; further improvement is necessary today, but possible.

runners_data.name: Largy Meadow
runners_data.note: Improving hold-up performer off career-best Newcastle second but needs significant luck from back of field
runners_data.comment: Went close at Newcastle recently and drying conditions would aid his cause
runners_data.spotlight: Improved form when 16-1 runner-up at Newcastle (2m4f, good) 12 days ago on second handicap start; needs to back up that latest performance but he's unexposed on good ground and drying conditions would aid his cause.

runners_data.name: La Vish
runners_data.note: Unexposed handicap newcomer whose hold-up style creates tactical issues despite recent Warwick success
runners_data.comment: Outsider of three when winning Warwick novice; the strength of that form is questionable
runners_data.spotlight: He was the 20-1 outsider of three when winning a novice at Warwick (2m5f, good) four weeks ago on his third hurdle start; this 5yo handicap newcomer is unexposed but the strength of that latest form is questionable given the heavily odds-on favourite severely underperformed.

runners_data.name: Monaco Rules
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 150-day absence with question marks over current form and fitness
runners_data.comment: French hurdle winner who went close at Sedgefield in November; this is his first run since
runners_data.spotlight: French hurdle winner who is 0-7 in Britain but he went close at Sedgefield (2m4f, soft) last November when last seen; also effective on good to soft ground; could be in the mix if fully tuned up after a break.

runners_data.name: Bel Ombre
runners_data.note: Back-marker whose January Taunton win came from prominent position, now reverting to hold-up style off higher mark
runners_data.comment: Well-backed winner on handicap debut at Taunton in January & the form has worked out well
runners_data.spotlight: Well backed into 85-40 when winning by 3l on handicap debut at Taunton (2m3f, good to soft) in January; 10lb higher for this first run since but the form has worked out well and he could have plenty more left in the tank.

races.paceDynamic: Joeybottles will set the early pace with Kingston Narcissus and King Jon Oliver likely to track close behind in the opening exchanges. The confirmed front-runner Joeybottles should get an uncontested lead given his natural pace-setting style, creating a sustainable tempo that won't collapse. With most of the field comprising hold-up horses (A King Of Magic, Bois Guillbert, Platin Moon, Largy Meadow, La Vish, Monaco Rules, Bel Ombre), there will be significant traffic issues in behind as they all seek racing room from the final flight. This race shape clearly favors prominent racers who can position themselves in the first half of the field and avoid the inevitable scramble, with front-runners also benefiting from the uncontested lead scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner
scenarios.trigger: If Joeybottles gets an easy lead and sustainable fractions
scenarios.body: The confirmed pace-setter can dictate terms without pressure, controlling the race from pillar to post while the large pack of hold-up horses get in each other's way. His recent Bangor win proves he can sustain a gallop when allowed to bowl along in front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses can secure good positions tracking the leader
scenarios.body: Kingston Narcissus and King Jon Oliver avoid the traffic problems that will plague the hold-up brigade, positioning themselves perfectly to challenge from the final flight. Their forward-going styles prove crucial when the back-markers struggle for racing room.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finds Gap
scenarios.trigger: If one of the many hold-up horses gets a clear run through
scenarios.body: Despite the tactical disadvantage, a well-handicapped hold-up horse like A King Of Magic or La Vish finds daylight when others are still stuck behind beaten horses. The winner needs both ability and significant luck to overcome the positional deficit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Joeybottles stops quickly or gets headed early in the straight
scenarios.body: An unsustainable early gallop or the leader tying up creates a more conventional finish where the stronger stayers can close from off the pace. This scenario requires the front-runner to weaken dramatically given his usual finishing kick.

watchPoints.text: Joeybottles getting headed or pressured early would completely change the race dynamic and favor the hold-up horses
Kingston Narcissus and King Jon Oliver securing tracking positions behind the leader as this determines the prominent challenge
The large group of hold-up horses (A King Of Magic, La Vish, Monaco Rules, Bel Ombre) getting decent positions turning in
Platin Moon's positioning early given his switch from front-running to hold-up tactics under new jockey Bruce Lynn
Any signs of unsustainable pace from Joeybottles in the opening mile could set up the back-markers perfectly

runners_data.name: Timefortom

runners_data.comment: Pulled up latest but has potential off opening mark if tapping back into earlier promise
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner who was runner-up this season on his first two hurdle starts (2m5f/2m4f, good/soft); pulled up at Newcastle (2m4f, good to soft) in January but has had a break since and he has potential off his opening mark if tapping back into his earlier promise.

runners_data.name: Stoner's Choice
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose mark is falling but course winner lacks a victory since April 2023
runners_data.comment: Course winner whose mark continues to fall but this 11yo is winless since April 2023
runners_data.spotlight: Course winner whose mark continues to fall and he's not been devoid of spark this season; however, this 11yo is without a win since April 2023 and was disappointing at Ludlow last month.

runners_data.name: Letterston Lily
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare returning after 524 days absence but lightly raced with strong course form when fit
runners_data.comment: Absent since November 2024 but on a competitive mark and one to watch in the betting
runners_data.spotlight: This is her first run since November 2024 and she needs to prove how much ability she retains; however, this lightly raced 6yo is on a competitive judged on her handicap form in autumn 2024 and it will be interesting to see how she goes in the betting on her return to action.

runners_data.name: Heard That
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won over fences here and was second in similar company at Southwell last month
runners_data.comment: Won off 7lb higher over fences here last April; 2nd over hurdles at Southwell last month
runners_data.spotlight: Won off 7lb higher over fences here (3m, good to soft) last April; 0-9 over hurdles but runner-up in this discipline at Southwell (2m4f, good) last month; one of two for trainer with a good record in the race; chance.

runners_data.name: Lets Mingle
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 100 days but won course and distance maiden and placed on handicap debut
runners_data.comment: Below par on her last two starts but lightly raced and today's conditions could help
runners_data.spotlight: Won C&D maiden (good) last May and runner-up on handicap debut at Kelso (2m6f, good) in October; below par on her next two runs but one was over 3m and the latest was on heavy going; this trip on drying ground could prove ideal and she's a possible contender.

runners_data.name: Buy Some Time
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who may have needed his comeback run at Kelso three weeks ago after long absence
runners_data.comment: Soundly beaten at Kelso recently but may have needed it; handy mark on last April's form
runners_data.spotlight: Soundly beaten at Kelso three weeks ago but may have needed that first run since last July; won a big-field handicap at 50-1 at Punchestown (2m3f, yielding) last April and is on a handy mark on that form; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Gentleman Bill
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer well handicapped on chase form but has been finishing down the field recently
runners_data.comment: Well handicapped on this season's chase form but down the field on his last two starts
runners_data.spotlight: Promising over hurdles last season and he's well handicapped on his chase form from the end of last year; however, he's finished down the field over fences/hurdles on his last two starts; blinkers replace cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: So Many Roads
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying bottom weight who won twice in Class 5 company but steps up in grade
runners_data.comment: 9yo who goes back up in grade today but ran well last time and is not ruled out each-way
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Ayr (2m4f, soft) in January and again ran well when fourth of 14 at Hexham (2m4f, soft) last month; those were Class 5 contests and this 9yo is back up in grade today, but is not ruled out each-way.

runners_data.name: Karton Plein
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who returned to form with third at Lingfield but pulled up last time out
runners_data.comment: Third at Lingfield in January; pulled up at Southwell since but he's not written off
runners_data.spotlight: Won a maiden hurdle at Southwell (2m, good to soft) last February and he returned to form when third at Lingfield (2m3f, soft) in January; pulled up at Southwell (2m4f, good) since but not written off for a trainer who has a good recent record in this race; one of two for the yard.

runners_data.name: Soldier's Leap
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won twice in autumn and was close second at Stratford last time
runners_data.comment: 1l second at Stratford last month and he can be in the mix if seeing out this longer trip
runners_data.spotlight: Won two in a row in the autumn (2m2f/2m, good to soft/soft) and, after a couple of respectable fifth placings, he was a close second at Stratford (2m2f, good) last month; in the mix if seeing out this longer trip; the hood worn on his last four starts is left off.

races.paceDynamic: Timefortom will take them along from the front without serious pressure, as the only confirmed lead horse in the field. Stoner's Choice and Lets Mingle will sit prominent but neither has early pace to challenge Timefortom's position through the early stages. The race will develop into a tactical affair with the large contingent of hold-up horses (Letterston Lily, Heard That, Buy Some Time, Gentleman Bill, So Many Roads, Karton Plein, Soldier's Leap) all looking to mount late challenges. This pace shape strongly favours the hold-up horses who can benefit from the sustainable gallop and time their runs from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Victory
scenarios.trigger: If Timefortom sets his usual honest gallop without getting into a speed duel early
scenarios.body: The pace will be perfect for the back-markers to unleash finishing kicks, with plenty of horses still on the bridle turning for home. The large number of hold-up performers creates multiple threats but also gives the best finishers clear winning opportunities.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses fail to put serious pressure on Timefortom and the hold-up brigade leave their runs too late
scenarios.body: Timefortom gets an easy lead and has enough left in the tank to resist late challenges, particularly given his proven stamina at this trip. The lack of early pace pressure allows him to dictate terms throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Stoner's Choice or Lets Mingle can get into the perfect stalking position and time their move perfectly
scenarios.body: The race becomes tactical with the prominent horses able to cover moves from the hold-up horses while still having Timefortom in their sights. This requires precise riding but the tactical nature could suit experienced campaigners.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Timefortom goes too slowly even for his standards and the race becomes a sprint from the last hurdle
scenarios.body: The entire field arrives together at the business end creating a cavalry charge finish where class and recent form become crucial. This chaotic finish could throw up any result but favours horses with tactical speed.

watchPoints.text: Timefortom could get an uncontested lead given the lack of early pace in this field
Letterston Lily faces a major fitness test on her first run since November 2024 after 524 days off
Buy Some Time may have needed his comeback run at Kelso and could strip fitter for this second start
The large number of hold-up horses could create traffic problems in the straight if they all come with runs together
Stoner's Choice is a course winner whose falling mark might finally hit his competitive level

runners_data.name: Tommy's Oscar
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who thrives off strong pace, recent Carlisle win suggests return to form, excellent record in similar conditions.
runners_data.comment: Won at Carlisle then fourth in stronger race than this at Haydock last week; in the mix
runners_data.spotlight: 11yo who snapped a losing sequence at Carlisle (3m, good to soft) last month and it was a stronger race than this in which he was fourth of 11 at Haydock (2m4f, good) last Wednesday; every chance he'll be in the mix.

runners_data.name: Classic Maestro
runners_data.note: Consistent front runner whose style will ensure honest gallop, 47 days off but trainer in good form with 4/24 recent record.

runners_data.name: King Roly
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with excellent course record including two C&D wins, ran here just yesterday so fitness guaranteed.
runners_data.comment: Has a very solid record here and could play a leading role if fully tuned up after a break
runners_data.spotlight: Made a good start to his chasing career last year, winning three times between May and September (2m3f/2m4f, good), with two of them over C&D; also effective on good to soft, unproven on softer; he has a very solid record here and could play a leading role if fully tuned up after a break.

runners_data.name: Toothless
runners_data.note: Natural leader from Paul Nicholls yard, won at Windsor on good ground, 47-day break shouldn't hinder front-running style.
runners_data.comment: Won at Windsor in January and runner-up to progressive winners on next two starts
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Windsor (2m4f, good) on New Year's Day on second start back from an absence and runner-up to progressive winners on next two starts (2m4f, soft); could still have more to offer himself and he's high on the list.

runners_data.name: Westerninthepark
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs strong pace to be effective, trainer Olly Murphy has 9/43 strike-rate suggesting yard in form.
runners_data.comment: Major turnaround needed but he's on a dangerous mark and trainer has excellent record here
runners_data.spotlight: Disappointing on his last few starts and a major turnaround is necessary; however, he's dropped to a dangerous mark and his trainer has an excellent strike-rate at Perth; no surprise if he bounces back.

runners_data.name: Whistleinthedark
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up performer with three Perth visits, recent form concerning but 11-year-old experience could prove valuable.
runners_data.comment: He's struggled on his last two starts but three visits to Perth have yielded two wins
runners_data.spotlight: 11yo who was tailed off at Cheltenham in December and pulled up at Haydock this month on sole run since; arrives with something to prove but three visits to Perth have yielded two wins, including this race in 2023, so he's worth a second look; a first-time visor replaces cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Slanagaibhgoleir
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from Gordon Elliott stable, good recent form including Down Royal win, Harry Cobden booking significant.
runners_data.comment: Some good form in this first chasing campaign; didn't stay 3m4f in Ulster National latest
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Down Royal (2m4f, good to yielding) in December and ran well in defeat on next two starts (2m3f/2m4f, heavy/good to yielding) prior to failing to stay 3m4f in the Ulster National at Downpatrick; could play a leading role back down in trip.

runners_data.name: Inox Allen
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 82-day break, previous C&D winner in first-time visor but current form disappointing.
runners_data.comment: C&D winner; hard to fancy on his 3 runs this term but change of headgear could be a plus
runners_data.spotlight: Easily made all in first-time visor over C&D (good to soft) last April; hard to fancy on his three runs this term but, given his previous reaction to new headgear, it's possible cheekpieces will garner a positive response.

races.paceDynamic: Classic Maestro and Toothless are confirmed front runners who will contest the early pace, with King Roly likely to take a prominent position just behind. This ensures a genuine gallop from the start over 2m4f, preventing the race from becoming a sprint finish. The honest tempo will stretch the field and test stamina reserves in the final half-mile. This pace scenario clearly favours hold-up horses who can benefit from the strong gallop and deliver late kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Classic Maestro and Toothless duel early and the pace stays strong throughout
scenarios.body: The honest gallop sets up perfectly for closers like Tommy's Oscar and Westerninthepark to deliver their finishing kicks. Front runners tire from their exertions allowing patient rides to prevail.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Gets Perfect Trip
scenarios.trigger: If King Roly tracks the leaders without getting embroiled in pace battles
scenarios.body: His good course record and proven ability at this trip allows him to strike when the front runners weaken. The strong early pace softens up his main dangers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders gets an uncontested lead while the other struggles early
scenarios.body: Classic Maestro or Toothless could dictate terms and have enough left for the finish. Without genuine pace pressure they can control the race tempo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If both front runners disappoint and fail to make the running as expected
scenarios.body: The race becomes tactical and turns into a sprint finish favouring horses with quick finishing kicks. This would be the least likely given both leaders' consistent front-running styles.

watchPoints.text: Classic Maestro and Toothless both missing the break or failing to make running would completely change race dynamics
King Roly looking tired from yesterday's exertion at Perth as fitness could be compromised by quick turnaround
Tommy's Oscar getting prominent position early would negate his hold-up style and preferred racing pattern
Westerninthepark showing early speed as hold-up horses need to be positioned for late runs in strongly-run races
Inox Allen responding positively to return to headgear as previous visor success suggests equipment change could spark improvement

runners_data.name: Minella Drama

runners_data.comment: Very useful at best; good second over 2m7f at Kelso in February; on a good mark now

races.paceDynamic: Minella Drama and If Not For Dylan will contest the early lead as two confirmed front runners, creating an honest gallop from the outset over this 3-mile trip. The pace will be testing but not suicidal, with both leaders capable of sustaining their effort, though Minella Drama's class advantage may see him dictate terms. Behind them, prominent racers Della Casa Lunga, Mountain Mike and American Mike will track the pace, while hold-up horses Statuario and Ned Tanner will need the race to develop into a stamina test. This shape strongly favours the front runners and prominent racers who can secure good positions early, as the genuine pace will stretch the field and make it difficult for hold-up horses to make up significant ground in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Minella Drama or If Not For Dylan can dictate terms without excessive early pressure
scenarios.body: The leader will have enough left to repel challenges, with the testing pace suiting those who travel smoothly in the front rank. Class will tell as the race develops into a staying test from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the two leaders go too fast early and weaken approaching the final circuit
scenarios.body: Della Casa Lunga or American Mike can strike from their tracking positions as the pace collapses ahead of them. Their prominent style allows them to avoid trouble while being close enough to capitalize.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Challenge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is moderate and the race becomes tactical
scenarios.body: Statuario can use his course experience and strong finishing kick to overcome the deficit created by his hold-up style. His six course wins demonstrate his ability to time his challenge perfectly at Perth.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Battle
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes a true staying test with multiple horses still in contention at the last
scenarios.body: The 3-mile trip and good ground will favor those with proven stamina reserves over the distance. Mountain Mike's inexperience at this level may be exposed despite his stamina.

races.paceDynamic: Adonedeal, The Hatchet, and Scriabin will ensure a strong gallop from the outset, with all three natural front-runners likely to dispute the early lead over this 2m trip. The pace will be searching throughout, particularly with The Hatchet having won over course and distance and Adonedeal needing to bounce back from a poor handicap debut. This sustained gallop will test stamina reserves in the closing stages and create opportunities for hold-up horses to finish strongly. The race shape strongly favours hold-up performers who can settle off the pace and produce their best work when others are tiring.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners maintain a genuine gallop throughout
scenarios.body: The searching pace will find out the stamina of the leaders and create ideal conditions for hold-up horses to strike late. Hold-up horses with proven stamina will have the tactical advantage as the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters breaks clear and sustains the gallop
scenarios.body: The winner gets first run on the field and maintains just enough in reserve to hold off late challengers. The strong early pace still tests the field but the winner has the class to cope.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners position perfectly behind the early pace
scenarios.body: A horse tracking the leaders gets the perfect trip and kicks when the front-runners weaken. The sustained gallop sets it up ideally for a horse that can sit handy and pounce.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go too fast and all three tie up badly
scenarios.body: The entire complexion changes as all the pace-setters fade dramatically, leaving the race to be won by whoever has anything left. This creates a muddling finish where any running style can prevail.

races.paceDynamic: Malangen is the only confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner field and faces no obvious early pressure, allowing him to dictate terms from the front. With most rivals adopting hold-up tactics (Tigress Lilly, Shadowfax Of Rohan, Game Beaaa, Canavan, Bunker Bay, Storm The Dug, Sao Carlos, Beat The Retreat, Bray Dale, Breaking Ground, Defying Gravity), the early pace will likely be steady rather than searching. This creates a tactical race where the tempo could quicken dramatically from the final flight as the large pack of hold-up horses makes their challenge. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can avoid traffic problems, while hold-up horses face the significant disadvantage of getting a clear run in such a crowded field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Malangen Controls Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Malangen gets an uncontested lead and maintains stamina over 2m
scenarios.body: The 11-year-old Perth specialist dictates throughout and has enough left to repel late challenges, with prominent racers best placed to follow him home. His four Perth wins and course knowledge prove decisive in a slowly-run tactical affair.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Benefits Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the large pack of hold-up horses gets bunched up turning for home
scenarios.body: Early leaders and prominent racers gain crucial positional advantage while the majority struggle for racing room in the final quarter-mile. Those avoiding the scramble capitalize on cleaner passages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Quality
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens significantly from three out and class tells
scenarios.body: Higher-rated hold-up horses like Game Beaaa and Beat The Retreat find gaps and use superior ability to reel in the leaders. Their class and finishing kick overcome positional disadvantages in a truly-run race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise From Outsiders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and stamina becomes secondary
scenarios.body: Lightly-weighted horses at the foot of the handicap like Bunker Bay and Breadalbane Lass benefit from the weight concession when the race becomes a sprint. Their low weights prove telling in a tactical finish.

races.paceDynamic: Burgundy Man is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate from flag to finish without pressure, creating a sustainable gallop over the 3m trip. William Of York, Loulou Madrik, Jakana and Uptown Harry can track in prominent positions, but none are aggressive enough to challenge Burgundy Man for the lead. The majority field comprises hold-up horses including Lady In The Park, Casual Observer, Inis Oirr, Nights In Venice, Sir Carnegie and Jirko who will rely on late surges. This uncontested pace scenario strongly favours prominent runners who can position close enough to strike when the pace inevitably slows, while hold-up horses face the risk of the race not developing into the sprint finish they require.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Burgundy Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Burgundy Man sets steady fractions without early pressure from the prominent group
scenarios.body: The pace becomes too modest for the hold-up brigade to reel in, allowing prominent trackers to move into contention turning for home. Those positioned second or third in the running order can time their move perfectly when Burgundy Man begins to tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Hold-Up Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses fail to capitalize on their position and the pace becomes pedestrian throughout
scenarios.body: The race sets up perfectly for the stronger stayers to unleash late kicks from the back, with the 3m trip suiting their stamina reserves. Quality hold-up performers can overcome poor positioning when the pace collapses completely.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Burgundy Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Burgundy Man's recent course and distance win translates to superior fitness and the field fails to mount a serious challenge
scenarios.body: The front runner maintains his advantage throughout, particularly if his October course victory indicates he has the track sussed. No horse shows enough early pace to apply meaningful pressure, allowing him to control the race completely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Royale
scenarios.trigger: If William Of York and Loulou Madrik decide to press Burgundy Man from early stages, creating genuine pace pressure
scenarios.body: The increased gallop suits the better class horses who can handle a true test, while the modest pace specialists struggle with the stepped-up tempo. This creates opportunities for horses with tactical speed who can adapt to faster fractions.

watchPoints.text: Burgundy Man getting an uncontested lead - if no prominent horse challenges early, he could steal this at soft fractions
Loulou Madrik's jumping - still relatively inexperienced over fences and any mistakes could ruin prominent positioning plans
Jakana's attitude after three consecutive pull-ups - first run without headgear in 63 days could see improvement or continued problems
Lady In The Park's response to first-time cheekpieces - defending champion needs something to spark improvement after poor season
The 10lb claiming jockeys on Inis Oirr and Jirko - inexperienced riders could struggle with tactical positioning in competitive handicap
